judged_text: When credential sharing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from the sync endpoint, but line 94 reads res?.data — a fetch Response has no data property — so token is undefined and line 95's token.access_token throws TypeError. Any self-hoster running the exact configuration this PR adds (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED + CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set) has every Google Calendar token refresh throw, completely breaking Google Calendar sync under the feature.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` it returns the raw `fetch(...)` result (a WHATWG `Response`). But in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the caller treats the return as a Google/gaxios response and does `const token = res?.data;` and then reads `token.access_token`/`token.expiry_date`. A `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` will be `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw at runtime under the enabled configuration. The diff shows no `.json()` (or similar) conversion in `refreshOAuthTokens` to make this compatible.
